title.narrative: Transition towards low and no-emission Electric Mobility in Azerbaijan

description.narrative: Note: Disbursement data provided is cumulative and covers disbursement made by the project Agency.
The project aims to promote low carbon, low-emission and integrated electric transportation systems in Azerbaijan, to reduce GHG emissions and improve air quality.

The project encompasses a range of socio-economic co-benefits. By investing in charging infrastructure across the country, including in remote and underserved areas, the project addresses a significant barrier to e-mobility adoption. This investment ensures that owners of electric and hybrid vehicles (currently 44,000 people, but the number will increase) will have better access to EV charging infrastructure, leading to improved connectivity and mobility options. Residents in remote regions will benefit from enhanced accessibility and equitable access to transportation services, promoting social inclusion. Moreover, by reducing reliance on traditional fossil fuel-powered vehicles, another co-benefit of the project is its contribution to improved air quality and public health outcomes. Road transport in Azerbaijan significantly contributes to local air pollution, with total emissions of harmful substances reaching 821 thousand tons annually, or approximately 81 kg per capita. Among these pollutants, in year 2023 carbon monoxide (CO) emissions stand at 556 thousand tons, nitrogen oxides (NOx) at 104 thousand tons, and hydrocarbons at 145 thousand tons. These emissions are detrimental to both public health and the environment, contributing to respiratory diseases, smog formation, and degradation of air quality. Transitioning to e-mobility, offers a promising solution to reduce these harmful impacts. By replacing conventional vehicles with EVs, which produce zero tailpipe emissions, Azerbaijan can lower the levels of CO, NOx, and hydrocarbons in the atmosphere, improving air quality and mitigating the transport sector's negative effects on the local environment. In addition, the project will lead to significant socio-economic benefits by lowering healthcare costs associated with pollution-related illnesses and improving the overall quality of life for residents. The widespread adoption of EVs supports environmental sustainability and can stimulate economic growth by creating new jobs in the green technology and infrastructure sectors. For example, the BYD project is expected to create 800 new jobs through the establishment of electric bus production facilities at the Sumgayit Chemical Industrial Park. This will not only stimulate local economic growth but also foster the development of skills in green technology. Moreover, the project's focus on training and capacity building plays a crucial role in enhancing human capital development and fostering economic growth. By providing training programs and technical expertise in e-mobility technologies and strategies, the project equips specialist communities with the skills and knowledge needed to participate in the growing electric vehicle industry. This not only creates employment opportunities and stimulates economic activity but also positions Azerbaijan as a leader in sustainable transportation solutions, potentially attracting investment and driving innovation in the e-mobility sector. Additionally, the project's emphasis on environmental sustainability and end-of-life treatment policies for EVs underscores Azerbaijan's commitment to responsible resource management and green growth, which can further enhance its reputation as a forward-thinking and environmentally conscious nation, attracting investment and fostering international partnerships for sustainable development initiatives.
